thread:
lucy: hitting weird ordering on Android webview onboarding. stream arrives but some mid-chunks are missing or jump out of order after a websocket->sse fallback. app shows garbled assistant text.
dan: websocket->sse fallback? we normally start SSE then upgrade to http/2-ish? which transport combo is this happening on?
lucy: flow: webview tries ws first (fast path) but webview blocks ws on some carriers, so we fallback to an xhr+sse shim. repro is flaky: open sample app in webview, start stream, toggle airplane mode for ~2s then restore. On restore the UI concatenates fragments in wrong order: chunk N+2 shows before N+1.
matt: could be buffering in the shim where fragments from the previous connection get queued and then interleaved with new ones on reconnect. Do we tag fragments with sequence numbers?
lucy: current shim uses implicit ordering based on arrival, no explicit seq. Logs: 
```
[net] conn=1 established via ws
[net] conn=1 -> blocked by carrier
[net] fallback to sse-shim, conn=2
[shim] buffer append: frag@offset=1024 len=512
[shim] buffer append: frag@offset=1536 len=400
[net] conn=2 resume, replay buffer
[shim] emit frag offset=1536
[shim] emit frag offset=1024  <-- out of order
```
zahid: wow emit order reversed. looks like our circular buffer read pointer is being reversed when we switch code paths. Any differences between ws and sse framing that could affect offsets?
matt: ws fragments are framed with explicit boundaries; sse uses data events and we normalize into a buffer. The shim glues boundaries together and uses a deque; maybe our pop_front/pop_back logic got flipped when we added a fast-path optimization.
dan: can you reproduce deterministically? if so capture a minimal HAR or turn on verbose shim logging. Also include a checksum/hash of each fragment so we can ensure content boundaries.
lucy: I can repro 7/10 on my Pixel 6 emulator with carrier sim. I'll add debug logs and sequence stamps. Quick hack: add fragment-seq header in the shim and drop any out-of-order fragments in consumer. But dropping might lose content; better to reorder on seq.
matt: agree reorder by seq on client. Server can't help here since fallback path might rewrite framing. We should: 1) stamp seq at the shim boundary (when converting network frames to fragments), 2) on replay/reconnect, sort buffered fragments by seq before emit, 3) add a parity-check in sample apps to validate sequences.

zahid: small note: sorting by seq introduces latency if fragments are delayed; use a small re-order window (e.g., wait up to 30ms for missing seq) then emit to avoid stalls. Make it configurable.
lucy: good point. will implement reorder-window with default 20ms and a debug toggle. I'll also push a unit test that simulates interleaved arrivals.
dan: add an e2e test in the webview sample harness that toggles network and asserts ordering on output tokens. That'll catch regressions.
matt: once we have seqs stamped, we can also expose them in logs for support to correlate with server logs. Add a small doc blurb in SDK release notes about the change.
bot-ci: heads up: if you modify sse-shim files, run `yarn test:shim` and `npm run e2e:webview` before landing.
lucy: will do. i'll open a small PR with seq stamping + reorder-window and mark it WIP. tagging @matt for review. thanks :rocket:
